main_topics.reason: The user opened with daily nausea after starting Ozempic and the conversation centred on managing it and when to worry.
The user asked directly whether it is safe to stop for some days, and said they almost stopped that day.
The user feared the nausea getting worse at the next dose and learned they can ask to delay the increase, which gave relief.
The user described fried food, meat and night-time worsening, and discussed small bland meals over several turns.
The user asked when the nausea is not normal and they should see a doctor fast, and confirmed they have none of the signs.
The user asked whether the drug is working and shared morning readings falling from 140-150 to around 120.
The user said they were scared of how bad it would get at a higher dose, mentioned once.
The user agreed to tell the doctor about the nausea and ask to wait before increasing, which came up near the end.

output.summary: A user three weeks into Ozempic had daily nausea and asked whether to stop, after their wife suggested it. The bot explained the side effect, gave meal tips, advised against stopping on their own, said the dose increase can be delayed, and listed warning signs. The user decided to keep going, check morning sugars and talk to their doctor, and said they felt calmer.
